patients.summary: Retired physics professor who joined in 2017 with hypertension, type 2 diabetes, CKD 3a and left hip arthritis. Mild cognitive impairment in 2020, a resected mucin-producing pancreatic adenocarcinoma with transient DIC in 2023, flash pulmonary edema and an anterior STEMI in 2024, E. coli septic shock he survived in 2025, and a right MCA stroke in April 2026 after his last practice visit.

documents.title: New patient inquiry
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Mr. Gallo phoned. His internist of many years has retired and the office is closing; a neighbor gave him our number. Retired from the university, Medicare plus a supplement plan. Says he has blood pressure and diabetes, both 'behaving'. Booked new patient appointment 9/12 at 9:00. Release form for his old office mailed to the house; asked him to bring every pill bottle to the visit.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
66 y/o man transferring care; his longtime internist retired this summer. Brought a shopping bag of bottles, which made reconciliation easy.

HTN since about 2006, lisinopril 10 for years, does not check at home. T2DM about 7 years, metformin 1000 BID, says last A1c was 'in the sixes'. Told a few years ago his kidney numbers were 'a little low' - CKD stage 3a per his account, no nephrology. L hip arthritis, aches after long walks, takes acetaminophen a few times a week, avoids ibuprofen because of an ulcer in the 1990s (treated, scoped back then, no bleeding since). Stays on omeprazole because he takes aspirin. Atorvastatin 40 and aspirin started by old doctor 'because of the diabetes'.

PSH: appendix out at 24, open incision.
FHx: father MI at 71. Mother T2DM, stroke at 76. Paternal uncle pancreatic cancer.
SHx: married, lives with wife in Florence. Daughter nearby, son lives in Germany. Retired university physics professor (PhD). Former smoker, about 20 pack-years, quit roughly 15 years ago. Alcohol a drink or two a month. Walks most days.
Allergies: NKDA.

ROS negative in detail apart from the hip.

Exam: BP and pulse as recorded. Pleasant, articulate, good historian. HEENT unremarkable. Neck supple, no thyromegaly, no bruits. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, healed RLQ scar. Ext without edema; L hip internal rotation a bit limited and uncomfortable at end range. Feet: skin intact, monofilament intact bilaterally, DP pulses 2+.

A/P
1. HTN - at goal on lisinopril 10. Continue.
2. T2DM - metformin 1000 BID. A1c, UACR today. Eye exam due - he has an optometrist.
3. CKD 3a - BMP today to set our own baseline. Keep NSAIDs off the table.
4. L hip OA - acetaminophen PRN, keep walking.
5. Remote PUD on aspirin - continue omeprazole.
6. Lipids/ASA - continue atorvastatin 40, aspirin 81.
7. HM - one-time HCV and HIV today. Will request old records for colonoscopy and vaccines. Former smoker age 65-75: AAA screening ultrasound ordered. Flu shot at nurse visit next month.

RTC 4 months.

documents.title: Records from prior internal medicine practice
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
Records received from patient's former internist (practice closing). 41 pages scanned. Summary for chart:
- Colonoscopy 06/2014: normal to the cecum, no polyps, prep good. Repeat interval 10 years.
- Tdap 05/19/2015. PCV13 10/04/2016.
- Problem list on their record: hypertension, type 2 diabetes, CKD stage 3a, L hip osteoarthritis, history of peptic ulcer.
- Last A1c on file 6.4 (spring 2017).
Originals to scanning.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Mr. Gallo, welcome again to the practice. Your labs are back. A1c 6.5, which is good control for you. Kidney function is in the same mildly reduced range your old office described, stable - no change needed, just the usual advice to skip ibuprofen and naproxen. Urine protein is normal. Cholesterol is well treated on the atorvastatin. Hepatitis C and HIV screens negative. See you for the flu shot next month.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Flu Vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: High-dose influenza 0.5 mL IM L deltoid. No prior reactions, VIS given. Tolerated. Reminded about the aorta ultrasound on the 26th - he had it on his calendar.

reports.text: Indication: AAA screening, male former smoker. Technique: grayscale and color imaging of the abdominal aorta from the diaphragm to the bifurcation. Findings: Proximal aorta 1.9 cm, mid 1.8 cm, distal 1.7 cm in AP outer-to-outer dimension. No aneurysmal dilation. Common iliac arteries normal in caliber. No periaortic fluid.
reports.conclusion: Normal caliber abdominal aorta. No abdominal aortic aneurysm.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Doing well over the winter. Walks at the indoor track when the roads are icy. No hypoglycemia (not expected on metformin alone). Hip about the same.
O: Vitals as charted. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. No edema.
A/P: BP higher than usual today - he rushed in from the parking lot; was fine in September. Recheck next visit. T2DM steady. A1c and BMP drawn. Meds unchanged. Next visit late spring.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your A1c and kidney panel from yesterday are in your usual range. No changes. Enjoy the indoor track.

documents.title: Refill request - 90-day supplies
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Mail-order pharmacy requesting new 90-day scripts with refills for lisinopril 10, metformin 1000, atorvastatin 40, omeprazole 20 (old prescriber retired). Sent per PCP standing approval, 90 days x 3 refills each.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Spring garden season - L hip complains after a day of digging and kneeling, settles overnight with two acetaminophen. Not limiting walks. No new issues otherwise; January A1c in his usual range.
Exam: BP fine today. L hip: mild discomfort with internal rotation, gait normal.
Plan: acetaminophen as he uses it, up to 3 g/day max; kneeling pad, break up the garden jobs. Avoid NSAIDs (ulcer history, kidneys). Physical in September.

documents.title: Diabetic eye examination - optometry
documents.author: optometry
documents.body: Comprehensive dilated eye exam, date of service 07/09/2018. Patient with type 2 diabetes. BCVA 20/25 OD, 20/25 OS. IOP normal OU. Lenses clear. Dilated fundus: no diabetic retinopathy OU, no macular edema. Recommend annual exam. Copy to primary care.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Initial Medicare AWV.
Functional: fully independent, still drives, manages own finances and medications (pillbox). No falls this year. Hearing and vision adequate; optometry July - no retinopathy.
Mood: PHQ-2 0. Cognition: no concerns from him or his wife; conversation sharp.
Safety: seat belt always, smoke detectors yes.
Advance directive: has a health care proxy (wife), will bring a copy.
Preventive: colonoscopy 2014 normal. AAA US 2017 normal. PCV13 2016 - PPSV23 today. High-dose flu today. Shingrix discussed, will do at nurse visits starting late fall.
Exam: vitals as charted. Unremarkable cardiopulmonary exam. Feet: monofilament intact, pulses good.
Labs drawn. Problems and meds reviewed - no changes.

documents.title: Physical labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: All of your physical labs look as expected: sugars well controlled, kidney function stable, cholesterol on target, blood count normal, no protein in the urine.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Shingrix #1
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Shingrix dose 1, 0.5 mL IM R deltoid. Counseled that a sore arm and a tired day afterward are common. Dose 2 due in 2-6 months, booked early February.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Quick visit. Arm was achy for a day after the Shingrix, nothing more. Diet loosened over the holidays, back on track now. Hip unchanged.
Exam: vitals reviewed, lungs clear, RRR, no edema.
Plan: A1c, BMP. Continue current regimen. Shingrix #2 on 2/7.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Shingrix #2
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Second Shingrix 0.5 mL IM L deltoid. Series complete. He asked for a printout of his vaccine record for his own files - given.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Back from three weeks visiting his son abroad, walked a great deal, hip held up. January A1c and creatinine at his usual.
No complaints. Exam unremarkable, BP at goal.
Continue all. Physical in the fall.

documents.title: Question about omeprazole
documents.author: patient
documents.body: I read an article suggesting long-term acid blockers may have downsides. My stomach has been quiet for twenty years. Can I stop the omeprazole? - R. Gallo

documents.title: RE: Question about omeprazole
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good question, and the article isn't wrong in general. In your case the omeprazole is there because you take a daily aspirin and you've had an ulcer before - that combination is exactly when it earns its keep. I'd stay on it. If we ever stop the aspirin we can revisit.

documents.title: Diabetic eye examination - optometry
documents.author: optometry
documents.body: Annual dilated exam 07/15/2019. VA cc 20/25 OU. Anterior segments normal. No diabetic retinopathy either eye. Return 1 year.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Subsequent AWV. Rescheduled from the August visit he cancelled.
Function: independent in ADLs and IADLs, drives, still referees a physics problem set for a former colleague now and then. No falls.
PHQ-2 0. Cognition: he says he is 'as absent-minded as any professor', no specific concerns raised.
Eye exam July - no retinopathy. Vaccines: high-dose flu today; pneumococcal and Shingrix complete; Tdap 2015.
Exam: vitals as charted, cardiopulmonary normal, feet intact.
Labs drawn. No medication changes.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Labs from Wednesday are back and steady across the board - A1c, kidney function, cholesterol and urine protein all where they have been.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Wife came along today. Both well. Fall labs fine - kidney function unchanged, LDL at goal, urine albumin normal.
BP at goal. Weight steady. Hip tolerable.
A1c drawn today. Continue regimen. RTC 2-3 months.
